name: US County Scoring System
unit: County-equivalent (counties, Louisiana parishes, Alaska boroughs and census areas, Virginia independent cities, Connecticut planning regions, DC); 2023 Census vintage, 3,144 units

scale.parameter: Every sub-parameter is scored 0-10 (one decimal). Unless a parameter says otherwise, score = 10 x national percentile rank of the raw metric, so 5.0 is the median US county.
scale.category: Category score (0-100) = 10 x weighted mean of its sub-parameter scores.
scale.signed: Parameters marked signed run -10 to +10 with 0 as the national reference point (used for partisan lean and trend).
scale.categorical: Parameters marked categorical store a label (e.g. dialect region, dominant tradition) alongside a 0-10 intensity score.
scale.smallCountyShrinkage: For rate metrics in counties under 5,000 residents, shrink toward the state mean before ranking: x_adj = (n*x + k*mu_state)/(n + k), k = 2,000.

categories.name: History
categories.description: How strongly each era of American history is imprinted on the county: population growth, surviving built environment, landmarks and defining events.
categories.eraImprintFormula: era_score = 10 x (0.40*G + 0.25*B + 0.20*L + 0.15*V), each term a 0-1 national percentile. G = share of the county's cumulative positive population growth that occurred in the era; B = share of surviving housing stock built in the era; L = NRHP listings whose period of significance falls in the era, per 100 sq mi and per 10k residents (mean of the two percentiles); V = curated event salience flag (0, 0.5 or 1).
categories.preCensusRule: Eras before 1790 have no census growth term. Reweight to 0.45*Settlement + 0.35*L + 0.20*V, where Settlement = 1 if a permanent European, African or colonial settlement (English, Spanish, French, Dutch, Swedish or Russian) existed in the county before the era ended, 0.5 if within the claimed but unsettled frontier, 0 otherwise.

parameters.name: Colonial America
parameters.note: Includes Spanish (St. Augustine 1565, Santa Fe 1610, California missions 1769+), French (Louisiana, Illinois Country, Detroit) and Russian (Alaska 1784+) colonial settlement, not only the 13 colonies.

parameters.name: America's founding years
parameters.note: Revolution through the War of 1812; Northwest Ordinance and Louisiana Purchase.

parameters.name: Industrial period
parameters.note: Reconstruction, Gilded Age, railroads, mass immigration and the Progressive Era reforms (1896-1917), which fall chronologically here.

parameters.name: Great Depression and New Deal (Progressive legacy)
parameters.note: Brief paired this era with the Progressive Era; Progressive reforms are scored in H04 and their New Deal continuation here.

parameters.name: Postwar boom and Civil Rights (added)
parameters.note: Not in the original brief. Added so WWII industry, suburbanization, the Interstates, Sun Belt growth and the Civil Rights movement have a home; set weight to 0 to remove.

parameters.name: Projections / future
parameters.note: 10 x (0.60*projected growth percentile + 0.25*(1 - climate risk percentile, FEMA NRI) + 0.15*(1 - water stress percentile)); 10 = strongest projected growth with low risk.

derived: history_depth (count of eras scoring 6 or more)
sources: Newberry Atlas of Historical County Boundaries
State demographer projections / UVA Weldon Cooper Center

categories.name: Jobs / Main Unique Positions
categories.description: What the county does for a living, how specialized it is, and which historic industries still define it.

parameters.name: Center of industry
parameters.metric: County share of national employment in its leading 3-digit NAICS industry (by location quotient, minimum 500 jobs). Score = 10 x percentile of log(share). Label = industry name.

parameters.name: Specialization
parameters.metric: 0.6 x percentile of the maximum location quotient (LQ = local industry share / national industry share, industries with 500+ jobs) + 0.4 x percentile of the Hirschman-Herfindahl concentration index across 2-digit NAICS sectors. Plus USDA ERS economic type label (farming, mining, manufacturing, federal/state government, recreation, nonspecialized).

parameters.name: Historical differentiators
parameters.metric: Legacy industry index: for each legacy industry (coal, metal mining, steel, textiles, autos, timber/paper, fishing, oil & gas, railroads, tobacco, cotton, ranching, shipbuilding, defense), persistence = min(1, current LQ / peak historical LQ) and magnitude = percentile of peak historical LQ. Score = 10 x max over industries of (0.5*magnitude + 0.5*magnitude*persistence). A high score with low persistence means a lost industry that still shapes identity.

sources: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
County and City Data Books 1947-1977 (historical LQ)

categories.name: Linguistic Regions
categories.description: Dialect membership from narrowest to most general scope, plus marked features and non-English language presence.

hierarchy.scope: Dialect region (Atlas of North American English)

parameters.name: Dialect assignment (L1-L3 labels)
parameters.metric: Labels from the ANAE map, with counties outside the surveyed cities assigned by nearest ANAE community within the same L2 region. Intensity = ANAE isogloss-bundle count passing through or enclosing the county, 0-10.

parameters.name: Marked features (L4)
parameters.metric: Weighted count of features present that differ from General American (see featureInventory). Score = 10 x (sum of weights present / max observed sum).

parameters.name: Non-English language presence
parameters.metric: Percentile of share of population 5+ speaking a language other than English at home; label = top non-English language.

parameters.name: Heritage / contact variety
parameters.metric: 0-10 curated: 10 = a distinct contact variety or Indigenous language is spoken by a substantial share (Gullah, Louisiana French, Pennsylvania Dutch, Hawai'i Creole, Navajo, Yup'ik, New Mexican Spanish); 5 = present in heritage or revival form; 0 = none.

featureInventory.desc: cot and caught sound the same
pin and pen sound the same
NYC / Philadelphia / Baltimore / New Orleans short-a system
pop / soda / coke recorded as a label, unweighted

sources: Labov, Ash & Boberg, Atlas of North American English (2006)
ACS table C16001 (language spoken at home)

categories.name: Religious Views
categories.description: Percent of people who identify with each religious tradition, how religious the county is overall, and how unusual its mix is.
categories.selfIdentificationMethod: County-level self-identification surveys do not exist. Estimate it by raking: start from the state self-identification shares (Pew Religious Landscape Study 2023-24, PRRI Census of American Religion), then scale each tradition by the county's congregational adherence rate for that tradition relative to the state's (US Religion Census 2020), and renormalize to 100%. Report both the adherence figure and the self-identification estimate.

parameters.name: % identifying with each tradition
parameters.metric: Vector of 11 shares (estimated self-identification). Label = largest tradition.

parameters.name: Religiosity
parameters.metric: Percentile of total congregational adherents per 1,000 residents.

parameters.name: Concentration
parameters.metric: Percentile of the Herfindahl index of tradition shares (high = one tradition dominates).

parameters.name: Distinctiveness vs national mix
parameters.metric: Dissimilarity index = 0.5 x sum of |county share - national share| across traditions, scored as a percentile.

categories.name: Environment
categories.description: Rural-urban character, terrain and physical divides, and other geographic factors.

parameters.name: Rural vs urban
parameters.metric: 0-10, 10 = most urban. 0.5 x (10 - (RUCC_2023 - 1) x 1.25) + 0.5 x 10 x percentile of log population density. Label = RUCC code.

parameters.name: Mountains and other divides
parameters.metric: 0.5 x percentile of local relief (standard deviation of elevation) + 0.5 x percentile of mean elevation. Labels: USGS physiographic division and province, side of the Continental Divide, side of the Cascade crest (WA/OR), Appalachian Regional Commission membership.

parameters.name: Climate and water
parameters.metric: Aridity: 10 x (1 - percentile of the P/PET aridity index), so 10 = most arid. Labels: Koppen climate class, desert name if any, HUC-2 river basin, Great Basin internal drainage flag.

parameters.name: Positional factors
parameters.metric: Labels (not scored): east/west/straddles the Mississippi, east/west of the 100th meridian, coastline (Atlantic, Gulf, Pacific, Great Lakes, Arctic, none), EPA Level III ecoregion. Score = federal land share percentile.

parameters.name: Hazard exposure
parameters.metric: Percentile of FEMA National Risk Index expected annual loss score. Label = top hazard.

categories.name: Voting History
categories.description: Partisan lean, direction of change, volatility, turnout and historical alignment.

parameters.name: Partisan lean
parameters.metric: Two-party Republican margin minus national two-party margin, averaged over 2016, 2020 and 2024 presidential elections (weights 0.25, 0.35, 0.40). Score = clamp(lean_points / 5, -10, +10). -10 = D+50 or more relative to nation, +10 = R+50 or more.

parameters.name: Trend
parameters.metric: OLS slope of relative margin per cycle, 2000-2024. Score = clamp(slope / 1.5, -10, +10); positive = moving Republican.

parameters.name: Volatility
parameters.metric: Percentile of standard deviation of cycle-to-cycle relative swing, 2000-2024.

parameters.name: Turnout
parameters.metric: Percentile of 2020-2024 average presidential votes / citizen voting-age population (ACS CVAP).

parameters.name: Historical alignment
parameters.metric: Party carried in the realignment benchmark elections 1896, 1932, 1964, 1980, 2008 and 2024, stored as a 6-letter string (e.g. 'DDDRDR'). Score = 10 x number of party switches between benchmarks / 5.

sources: MIT Election Data + Science Lab county returns 2000-2024
ICPSR 8611 / Dave Leip's Atlas (historical county returns)
caveats: Alaska reports presidential results by state house district, not by borough; allocate precinct results to boroughs before scoring.
Connecticut and New England results are reported by town; aggregate to planning regions / counties.

verification.name: Final verification (per capita and per area)
verification.description: Every count-based metric is computed three ways (raw, per 1,000 residents, per square mile) and checked before any score is accepted. Per square foot is supported as a display unit (per sq mi / 27,878,400) but scoring uses per square mile, because per-square-foot values for counties are too small to read.

checks.test: Spearman correlation of each parameter with log(population) and with log(area).
checks.rule: If |rho| > 0.6, the parameter is mostly measuring size: switch it to its per-capita or per-area form, or note why size is the point.

checks.test: Rate metrics in counties under 5,000 residents.
checks.rule: Apply the shrinkage rule from scale.smallCountyShrinkage; mark confidence no higher than B.

checks.test: Compare a county's rank on raw, per-capita and per-area versions of the same metric.
checks.rule: Top decile raw but below median per capita = 'scale-driven'; below median raw but top decile per capita = 'small-but-intense'. Both flags are reported, not hidden.

checks.test: z-score of each category score within the county's region.
checks.rule: |z| > 3 goes to manual review; confirmed outliers are kept and annotated.

checks.test: Benchmark counties with well-established expected results (see PARAMETERS.md).
checks.rule: Any benchmark landing outside its expected band blocks release of that category until fixed.

checks.test: Re-score with the previous data vintage.
checks.rule: A category moving more than 20 points without a documented real-world cause is investigated.

verification.confidenceGrade: A = all inputs county-level and current; B = some inputs shrunk, interpolated or state-derived; C = mostly curated or region-default values.

composite.categoryScores: history, jobs, linguistic, religion, environment, voting: each 0-100.
composite.compositeScore: Weighted mean of the six category scores using category weights (default equal). Treat as an intensity/distinctiveness index, not a quality ranking.
composite.regionalTypicality: Cosine similarity (0-1) between the county's vector of all sub-parameter scores and the mean vector of its assigned region. High = textbook example of the region; low = outlier or border county.
